messages.subject: Re: Error message with detectionHistory (error in cleanSubsetSpecies)
parts:
Hi Michael, 
there seems to be a discrepancy between the record dates and the camera operation dates. See the warnings:
  • record date before camera operation date range:  DL12 ...
  • 52 records out of 52 were removed ...
Without having seen the data it seems like all your records were before the camera setup date, which would result in an empty detection history. Can you share the output of the following lines please? It returns the first and last day each station was active (according to the camera operation matrix).

apply(camop_problem, MARGIN = 1, function(X){min(which(!is.na(X)))})    # 1st day of each station
apply(camop_problem, MARGIN = 1, function(X){max(which(!is.na(X)))})    # last day of each station

Alteratively please check the dates in the setup and retrieval columns of the camera trap station table that was used to create the camera operation matrix. Do they match the record dates?

Thank you,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error message with detectionHistory (error in cleanSubsetSpecies)
parts:
Hi Michael,
Thank you for the update. Can you please share your call of cameraOperation()? The probably has to to do with argument dateFormat in cameraOperation.
In the table you shared, the dates are in DD/MM/YYYY format. 
You could try to define dateFormat with the new functionality of using the lubridate package to define dates (since version1.2). For details see the vignette or ?cameraOperation.
In short, use 

dateFormat = "dmy"

or (the traditional way)

dateFormat = "%d/%m/%Y"

Does this help?
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Error message with detectionHistory (error in cleanSubsetSpecies)
parts:
Hi Michael,
the issue might be due to Excel. When you open a csv table in Excel and save it, date formats may change. This is because of the automatic date formatting that Excel does and then saves. So depending on your system settings, 2019-12-31 may become 31/12/2019 or something else, and the dateFormat argument in R needs to be changed.

Likewise, the date/time column in record tables may lose their seconds when saved in Excel. The original can be restored with the date and time columns which are provided separately in record tables.

Hence it is good practice to check the date format when loading data into R. Since this is a recurrent issue I'll see if I can find some sort of automatic check if the dateFormat provided by the user fits the data. 
Thank you for the feedback and feel free to let me know if there's more issues.
Best regards,
Jürgen
